scope: Characterize the inventory opcode family for FFXIV 1.23b. Catalogue Inventory*Packet wire types, cross-reference against existing BCS-Y coverage, classify each opcode against FUN_004DC690 dispatch (Patterns A-E), resolve or restate 0x0147 InventorySetEnd open question, and document the inventory data-flow into the PlayerBase/MyPlayer item-storage container.

inventory_data_flow_summary.egress: Inventory item updates land in the PlayerBase/MyPlayer storage vector at this+0x144 (BCS-Y-0414). The vector holds 4 ItemPackage buckets with capacities 0x23 / 0x41 / 0x1a / 0x04 (35 / 65 / 26 / 4 slots). Per-bucket records are 0x10 bytes and are appended via FUN_007228E0 / sorted via FUN_00720BB0 / capacity-reserved via FUN_007222D0. The EntrustItemReceiver worker FUN_006EFBD0 demonstrates the same bucket layout for the cross-receiver write path.
inventory_data_flow_summary.lua_surface: Lua-bound readers on Application::Lua::Script::Client::Control::ItemBase: _getItem, _getEquippingItem, _getItemPackageCapacity, _getItemPackageFreeSpace, _hasItemPackage, _isLockingItem, _isItemDealing, _getTradingItem. ItemManager vtable (VA 0x00FD7618) slot 1 = FUN_007036E0 fires _onUpdateItemPackage and _onUpdateTradingItem firers. ItemBase._updateWork = c2s opcode 0x0132 (BCS-Y-0383 / 0x132 was tentatively named ItemWorkUpdatePacket).
inventory_data_flow_summary.commit_pattern: Inventory mutations arrive in atomic batches gated by InventoryBeginChange (0x016d) -> InventoryListX01/08/16/32/64 (0x0148..0x014c) AND/OR InventoryRemoveX01/08/16/32/64 (0x0152..0x0156) AND/OR LinkedItemListX01..X64 (0x014d..0x0151) AND/OR InventorySetBegin (0x0146) -> InventoryEndChange (0x016e). 0x0147 InventorySetEnd appears to logically pair with 0x0146 InventorySetBegin (similar 8-byte empty payload, same 24-byte body length) but the client silently discards it.

c2s_counterpart.0x0131: UpdateItemPackagePacket (c2s) - client requests item-package state (retainer item listings, bazaar). Sent via FUN_0075EA50 builder; bound to CharaBase._updateItemPackage Lua N-API per BCS-Y-0382/0388. Payload is u32 actorID + u32 packageId; client emits u8 packageId only (FUN_0075EA50).
c2s_counterpart.0x0132: ItemWorkUpdatePacket (c2s, tentative) - bound to ItemBase._updateWork (BCS-Y-0383). Builder FUN_0075EAC0.
c2s_counterpart.note: There is NO 0x012E c2s inventory packet despite older pcap-mining heuristics suggesting so. The 0x012E c2s opcode is EventUpdatePacket (event family). The earlier memory note 'c2s vocab maps to inv=0x012E' was a size-based heuristic from the pcap-opcode-evidence pass that has since been refined - the inventory-shaped 120-byte c2s payload on 0x012E is actually event-framed inventory operations (EventUpdate wraps a Lua-param stream that includes inventory verbs); the underlying transport is still the EventStart/EventUpdate generic frame per docs/client-architecture.md, '1.x combat is asymmetric'.

key_findings: Inventory s2c subsystem comprises 17 unique opcodes (0x0146..0x014e, 0x014f..0x0151 linked-item variants, 0x0152..0x0156 remove variants, 0x016d, 0x016e). All but 0x0147 use Pattern direct_handler_in_FUN_004DC690.
11 of 17 inventory opcodes have decomp-backed payload structs already in unmapped_payload_decoding.json (covered by BCS-Y-0393 / 0394 / 0395 / 0396).

The 8 remaining handler-known-but-payload-inferred opcodes (0x014c, 0x014f, 0x0150, 0x0151, 0x0153, 0x0154, 0x0155, 0x0156) follow the same X01/X08/X16/X32/X64 record-array pattern as the decoded ones; decomp work is mechanical but only 0x0153 has any pcap samples (2) to validate against.

Inventory dispatch is NOT a Receiver-class pattern. None of the 17 inventory opcodes appear in receiver_opcode_map_inbound.json, consistent with the architectural finding that 'remaining s2c opcodes do not use the Receiver-class pattern'.

Inventory data flow goes through the PlayerBase/MyPlayer storage vector at this+0x144 (4 buckets x 0x10-byte records, capacities 0x23/0x41/0x1a/0x04) per BCS-Y-0414 InventoryStorageItemHandleLane2. The Lua surface is Application::Lua::Script::Client::Control::ItemBase (20 reader N-APIs) and Application::Lua::Script::Client::Control::ItemManager (vtable VA 0x00FD7618 slot 1 fires _onUpdateItemPackage / _onUpdateTradingItem).

c2s inventory traffic uses opcode 0x0131 UpdateItemPackagePacket (NOT 0x012E as an outdated memory note claimed; 0x012E is the event-family EventUpdatePacket). The earlier 'inv=0x012E' heuristic from the pcap-opcode-evidence pass was based on a 120-byte payload size that turned out to be event-framed inventory operations carried over the generic EventStart/EventUpdate frame per docs/client-architecture.md, '1.x combat is asymmetric'.

InventoryBeginChange (0x016d) + InventoryEndChange (0x016e) bracket atomic-batch mutations. The Begin callee (FUN_0076BAD0) sets the change state; the End callee (FUN_0076BB00) invokes the commit + fanout + ItemPackage cleanup chain. InventorySetBegin (0x0146) + InventorySetEnd (0x0147) appear to be the per-container analog of the same bracketing, but only the Begin side is consumed - again pointing to 0x0147 as a vestigial / NOP-on-client opcode.
